# ABOUT THE ANTIMICROBIAL COMPUTERIZED DECISION SUPPORT SYSTEM (CDSS)

The Antimicrobial CDSS is a tool within the Computerized Patient Record System that offers antimicrobial prescribing advice to clinicians at the point of order entry. The system is structured as an order menu decision tree that contains quick orders pre-programmed with appropriate antimicrobial regimens for specific infectious diseases.

# Goals

Improve patient outcomes, reduce rates of microbial resistance, prevent adverse patient outcomes, optimize costs and improve providers' lives. In addition to these goals, the program fulfills antimicrobial stewardship quality standards implemented by the Joint Commission.

# Rationale

*Improved patient outcomes
In a 2013 study, Minneapolis Veterans Affairs Medical Center (MVAMC) antimicrobial courses ordered through the Antimicrobial CDSS were significantly more likely to be appropriate from start to completion, (44%) compared to non- CDSS courses (33%, P = 0.013). This is consistent with other studies that have shown significant improvement in appropriate use of antimicrobials when CDSS programs are utilized.

*Restricted formulary
The Minneapolis VAHCS has a restricted antimicrobial formulary. A restricted formulary reduces cost of health care and is an integral part of antimicrobial stewardship. The Antimicrobial CDSS provides a method of formulary restriction that doesn't require a call back from pharmacy or a prior authorization for the antimicrobial to be approved.

[More information on antimicrobial restriction policy](restriction-policy)

*Increased efficiency
Along with being able to order restricted antimicrobials without a prior authorization or call back from pharmacy, the Antimicrobial CDSS provides quick orders pre-programmed with appropriate antimicrobial regimens for specific infectious diseases. Using the system saves time and increases the efficiency of the ordering provider.

# Features

The CDSS has been developed locally with input from a broad, representative group of clinicians. Recommendations have been based on local susceptibility patterns, clinical evidence, local preferences, and national guidelines. The CDSS provides a way for clinicians to select alternative drugs when the recommended drugs are contraindicated.
